remainder of the specimen consists of unremarkable yellow, lobulated adipose 
tissue (90%), and stranded fibrous tissue (10%). Representative sections, 
including all fibrous tissue, are submitted. Approximately 90% of the specimen

The tumor cells do not stain for progesterone receptor protein. See Note. Note: In this laboratory, the results of prospective staining for estrogen receptor protein of 100 unfixed breast tumors were compared with determinations of estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. 93% of tumors that reacted with this antibody were positive for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. 100% of tumors that failed to stain were negative for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. In this laboratory, we also compared the results of staining for progesterone receptor protein of 50 breast carcinomas with determinations of progesterone receptors by a hormone binding assay. Seventy-three percent of tumors that stained with this antibody contained progesterone receptors by the biochemical assay, and 91% of tumors that failed to stain lacked the receptors. Diagnosis by: Phuong Nguyen, MD Signed On: 25 REMOVED_MONTH 94 at 15:50 Consulting Pathologist(s): Nancy Lee Harris, M.D. =============================================================================== *** IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY Addendum *** RESULTS OF IMMUNOPEROXIDASE STAINS, FROZEN SECTIONS ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ): With antibodies to immunoglobulin (GMAD kappa lambda) there is monotypic (kappa light chain) staining of many tumor cells in a diffuse pattern. There is faint reactivity with antibodies to IgG and IgA heavy chains, but this staining pattern is somewhat equivocal and cannot be distinguished from background. With antibody to B-lineage antigen ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) there is a similar pattern to immunoglobulin. The B cells are negative with antibodies to  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID . With antibodies to T-lineage associated antigens ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) there is staining of many small cells scattered within the tissue. Together with the morphologic features on routine sections, these results confirm the diagnosis of malignant B-cell lymphoma and exclude a reactive lymphoid hyperplasia.
